artifact_under_review.note: the wheel ships the Cython sources (.pyx/.pxd) AND the generated C, so the seam can be read as source rather than inferred

the_seam.declaration: pyreadstat.py:56 `class FileLike(Protocol)` — public, typed, documented: 'Should work with any file-like object that has read and seek methods, such as those returned by open() or io.BytesIO'
the_seam.public_api_exposure: read_sav/read_dta/... accept `filename_path` typed as FilePathorBuffer; the docstring for the parameter reads 'path to the file or file-like object'
the_seam.detection: _readstat_parser.pyx:1252 `if hasattr(filename_path, 'read') and hasattr(filename_path, 'seek'):` -> `file_obj = filename_path`; `_readstat_parser.pyx:1254 filename_bytes = b""  # Empty path - will be ignored when file_obj is used`
the_seam.handler_selection: _readstat_parser.pyx:965 `if file_obj is not None:` installs ALL FOUR Python-bridge handlers and sets io_ctx to the file object:

handlers_installed.open: pyobject_open_handler — body is `"""File is already open - this is a no-op"""; return 0`  (pyx:867-869)
handlers_installed.close: pyobject_close_handler — `"""User manages file lifetime - this is a no-op"""; return 0` (pyx:871-873)
handlers_installed.read: pyobject_read_handler — `file_obj.read(nbyte)` then memcpy into the ReadStat buffer (pyx:875-887)

the_seam.parse_call: _readstat_parser.pyx:997/1001 `readstat_parse_sav(parser, filename, ctx)` / `readstat_parse_dta(...)` where `filename` is the EMPTY b"" on the broker route and the parser carries io_ctx = the file object
the_seam.source_backed_conclusion: On the broker route the compiled reader is handed an EMPTY path, its open handler is a no-op, and every byte it consumes arrives through the Python read callback. There is no path string available for a compiled path-open to act on, so the compiled reader performs NO separate source-path open on this route.
the_seam.evidence_grade: SOURCE (Cython source shipped in the installed wheel) + CONTROL FLOW + SYNTHETIC REPRODUCTION. Not inferred from inability to observe.

the_four_claims_under_attack.claim: a caller-supplied object with .read/.seek causes pyreadstat/ReadStat to use the Python bridge
the_four_claims_under_attack.basis: pyx:1252/965 source plus synthetic broker reproducing successfully; io.BytesIO (no fd, no path) also works

the_four_claims_under_attack.claim: the compiled reader receives no usable source path and performs no separate source-path open on that route
the_four_claims_under_attack.basis: empty filename b"" is passed; pyobject_open_handler is a documented no-op; io.BytesIO has no path or fd and still parses

the_four_claims_under_attack.claim: the application-owned open is therefore the complete literal O1-C07 source-path open at that route
the_four_claims_under_attack.basis: the app owns the only open; the bridge records every read/seek; no second open exists to account for on that route
the_four_claims_under_attack.caveat: this makes the literal account OBTAINABLE on the broker route; it does not by itself change any frozen budget

the_four_claims_under_attack.claim: reads/bytes become observable at the actual I/O owner
the_four_claims_under_attack.basis: measured read-call and byte totals at the broker for SAV and DTA (see 02)

private_or_public.finding: PUBLICLY TYPED AND DOCUMENTED in 1.3.6 — FileLike is an exported Protocol and the parameter docstring names 'file-like object'. It is not a private/underscore seam.
private_or_public.but: it is a thin, version-sensitive bridge. The handler bodies, the empty-path convention, and the exception-swallowing behaviour are implementation details that a future version could change without notice.
private_or_public.requirement: pin the exact pyreadstat build (1.3.6) and the host interpreter identity; re-qualify on any change. This is consistent with the R7 identity spine.
